finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after only checking that the hostname ends with the string 'example.com'. This check has no leading dot, so 'evilexample.com' passes. The ALLOWED_SUFFIX constant, which has the dot, is never used. Scheme and port are not restricted. A user can register a domain ending in example.com, or point one at an internal IP. Redirects are not followed by httpx by default, so they are not the main bypass. The response length is returned, which gives a blind oracle.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
host.endswith('example.com') with no dot boundary, so attacker-controlled evilexample.com passes
c.get(url) is sent to the attacker-chosen host, which can resolve to 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 or other internal addresses

finding.guards_checked: Only the endswith('example.com') hostname check. It has no dot boundary, and the intended ALLOWED_SUFFIX (.example.com) is unused. There is no scheme check, no IP or DNS resolution check, and no pinning of the connection address. The httpx default of not following redirects does not stop a direct request to an attacker-owned domain. The /ping endpoint uses a constant URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: Only host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13, which is a suffix check without a dot boundary and does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is unused. There is no scheme, IP or DNS check.
verdict.reason: mirror.py:11 takes the url query parameter and mirror.py:13 only checks endswith("example.com"), so evilexample.com passes and mirror.py:16 fetches it, returning the response length at mirror.py:17.
